title: Regular and Irregular Verb Forms
summary: Learn to choose past simple and past participle forms of regular and irregular verbs. Use the right form after have or be and in sentences about completed past actions.
learningObjectives: Make common regular past forms and past participles with the correct -ed spelling.
Recall familiar irregular past simple and past participle forms.
Tell a past simple form from a past participle in present perfect and passive sentences.
Choose accurately between irregular verbs whose past forms match and those whose forms differ.

explanation.heading: Three forms to recognise
explanation.body: It helps to learn a verb as a set of three forms: the base form, the past simple and the past participle. Use the past simple to report a finished past action. Use the past participle after have or has in the present perfect, or after a form of be in a passive sentence.
explanation.example: They chose the longer path last time. This time, they have chosen a shorter path.

explanation.heading: Regular verbs: usually add -ed
explanation.body: Most regular verbs have the same form in the past simple and past participle. Add -ed to many base verbs, add -d after a final e, and change consonant + y to -ied. Some short verbs double the final consonant before -ed, as in plan → planned.
explanation.example: We planned the picnic carefully, but the weather changed.

explanation.heading: Irregular verbs with matching past forms
explanation.body: Some irregular verbs use the same word for the past simple and past participle, even though it is not a regular -ed form. Examples include keep → kept → kept, sell → sold → sold and put → put → put. Learn these forms rather than trying to add -ed.
explanation.example: He sold his old desk. He has sold the chair too.

explanation.heading: Irregular verbs with different past forms
explanation.body: Other irregular verbs have one form for the past simple and another for the past participle. For example, take → took → taken, write → wrote → written and see → saw → seen. After have or has, choose the third form, not the past simple form.
explanation.example: Mae took the photograph. She has taken several more since then.

explanation.heading: Use the participle in passive sentences
explanation.body: A passive verb also needs the past participle after be. The form of be shows the tense: is repaired refers to a present passive, and was repaired refers to a past passive. For an irregular verb, remember the participle: was found, not was find or was finding.
explanation.example: The missing map was found behind a cupboard.

left.label: Regular: borrow
left.note: The past simple and participle both end in -ed.

right.label: Irregular: choose
right.note: The two past forms are different; do not add -ed.

left.label: Past simple
left.note: Wrote can stand as the main past-tense verb.

right.label: Past participle
right.note: Has needs the participle written rather than wrote.

examples.sentence: The gardener watered the plants before breakfast.
examples.note: Watered is the regular past simple of water.

examples.sentence: We have carried the boxes upstairs.
examples.note: Carry changes consonant + y to -ied: carried.

examples.sentence: I kept the receipt in my bag.
examples.note: Kept is the irregular past simple; the participle is also kept.

examples.sentence: The children have drawn pictures of the seaside.
examples.note: Draw has different past forms: drew and drawn.

examples.sentence: The old benches were replaced in spring.
examples.note: Were + replaced forms a past passive with a regular participle.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I have wrote the address down.
commonMistakes.correct: I have written the address down.
commonMistakes.why: Have requires written, the past participle of write.

commonMistakes.incorrect: She buyed a warm coat yesterday.
commonMistakes.correct: She bought a warm coat yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: Buy is irregular: its past simple is bought.
Plan doubles the final n before -ed.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The parcel was took to the front desk.
commonMistakes.correct: The parcel was taken to the front desk.
commonMistakes.why: The passive needs taken, not the past simple took.

studyTips: Keep a three-column list for common verbs: base form, past simple, past participle. Practise complete sentences with each form.
After have, has, was or were in a perfect or passive pattern, pause and check whether the third verb form is needed.
Group irregular verbs by pattern: kept/kept, took/taken and put/put are easier to remember together with similar verbs.

exercises.prompt: Last night, Nadia ___ a short email to the organiser.
exercises.feedback: Last night signals a finished past action, so use the past simple wrote.

exercises.prompt: The music stopped because someone ___ the speaker off.
exercises.feedback: Turn is regular; the past simple form is turned.

exercises.prompt: I've never ___ such a long letter.
exercises.feedback: Have needs the past participle written, not the past simple wrote.

exercises.prompt: The missing wallet was ___ behind the sofa.
exercises.feedback: The passive structure was + past participle needs found.

acceptedAnswers: visited
exercises.feedback: Visit is a regular verb: add -ed for the past simple.

exercises.prompt: I have ___ (take) the wrong bag by mistake.
acceptedAnswers: taken
exercises.feedback: Take → took → taken; after have, use taken.

acceptedAnswers: bought
exercises.feedback: Buy is irregular. Its past simple form is bought.

exercises.prompt: The pictures were ___ (hang) in the hallway last night.
acceptedAnswers: hung
exercises.feedback: The participle of hang for objects is hung; were hung is a past passive.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I have ate my lunch already.
acceptedAnswers: I have eaten my lunch already.
exercises.feedback: After have, use eaten, the past participle of eat.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: We goed home before it started raining.
acceptedAnswers: We went home before it started raining.
exercises.feedback: Go is irregular: its past simple is went.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Her cousins have catched the last bus.
acceptedAnswers: Her cousins have caught the last bus.
exercises.feedback: Catch → caught → caught; use caught after have.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The guide stoped near the bridge.
acceptedAnswers: The guide stopped near the bridge.
exercises.feedback: Stop doubles the final p before -ed: stopped.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say a past simple sentence from these cues: 'my brother / choose / a blue jacket / yesterday'.
acceptedAnswers: My brother chose a blue jacket yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: The past simple of choose is chose.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say a present perfect sentence from these cues: 'we / write / three postcards'.
acceptedAnswers: We have written three postcards.
We've written three postcards.
speakingExercises.feedback: Have requires the participle written; we've is a normal contraction.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say a past passive sentence from these cues: 'the window / repair / last Thursday'.
acceptedAnswers: The window was repaired last Thursday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use was + the regular past participle repaired.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say one complete past simple sentence with these details: Holly / carry / two boxes / upstairs / yesterday. Use every detail.
acceptedAnswers: Holly carried two boxes upstairs yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Carry becomes carried in the past simple: consonant + y changes to -ied.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change "Sam wrote a short note last night" to the present perfect. Keep "Sam" and "a short note", but remove "last night".
acceptedAnswers: Sam has written a short note.
Sam's written a short note.
speakingExercises.feedback: Write → wrote → written. After has, use the past participle written, not wrote.

speakingExercises.prompt: A friend asks what happened to a missing scarf. It was found under the bed this morning. Answer in one past passive sentence beginning "The scarf" and include the place and time.
acceptedAnswers: The scarf was found under the bed this morning.
speakingExercises.feedback: The past passive uses was + found, the irregular past participle of find.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct the spelling of the past verb without changing other words: "We stoped beside the lake."
acceptedAnswers: We stopped beside the lake.
speakingExercises.feedback: Stop doubles the final p before -ed: stopped.

speakingExercises.prompt: Tell a friend two facts in one sentence joined by but: you bought a camera yesterday, and you have not taken any photos yet. Begin with "I" and use bought and taken.
acceptedAnswers: I bought a camera yesterday, but I haven't taken any photos yet.
I bought a camera yesterday, but I have not taken any photos yet.
speakingExercises.feedback: Bought is the past simple of buy; taken is the participle of take after have not.

listeningExercises.audioText: Ellie sent three letters on Tuesday.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which form of send did the speaker use?
listeningExercises.feedback: Sent is the irregular past simple of send.

listeningExercises.audioText: The bicycle has been stolen from the garden.
listeningExercises.prompt: What do we learn about the bicycle?
choices: Someone is stealing it right now.
listeningExercises.feedback: Been stolen uses the irregular past participle stolen in a present perfect passive.

listeningExercises.audioText: After dinner, I washed all the cups.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the past simple form of the verb meaning 'clean with water' that you hear.
acceptedAnswers: washed
listeningExercises.feedback: Wash is regular; its past simple form is washed.

listeningExercises.audioText: The children have drawn a large map for their school project.
choices: A drawing for a school assignment
A written invitation to a party
listeningExercises.feedback: Have drawn says the children have completed a drawing; drawn is the past participle of draw.

listeningExercises.audioText: Yesterday, the gardener dug a small hole beside the gate.
listeningExercises.feedback: Beside the gate means near the entrance. Dug is the irregular past simple form of dig.

listeningExercises.audioText: I broke the cup yesterday, but I have already bought another one.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which statement matches the speaker’s situation?
choices: The cup has not been damaged.
The speaker still needs to buy another cup.
The cup broke in the past, and a new one has been purchased.
listeningExercises.feedback: Broke describes a completed past event; have bought uses the past participle bought to report a new purchase.

listeningExercises.audioText: Someone has taken the blue umbrella from the office.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the single past participle you hear immediately after the auxiliary.
acceptedAnswers: taken
listeningExercises.feedback: Take → took → taken. Present perfect has taken requires the participle taken.

listeningExercises.audioText: The team planned a short trip for Saturday.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the one-word past-tense verb describing what the team did.
acceptedAnswers: planned
listeningExercises.feedback: Plan doubles its final n before -ed: planned.
